newsitem.title: HUNGARY: AKK to take over Hungary foreign borrowing in 1998.
newsitem.headline: AKK to take over Hungary foreign borrowing in 1998.

text.p: Hungary's Government Debt Management Agency (AKK) said on Tuesday it expects to assume the task of borrowing for the country from abroad from mid-1998.
"We expect that from the middle of 1998 we will be the issuers," AKK Deputy Director Maria Dunavolgyi said.
Under the current system, the National Bank of Hungary (NBH) takes up the country's foreign loans and lends them on to the state budget.

But according a draft law approved by the government last week along with the draft 1997 budget, the central bank could not lend to the state budget from January 1, and the state budget will take over some 2,000 billion worth of Hungary's foreign loans from the central bank.
This aims at making the budget more transparent in order to meet the requirements of the European Union, which Hungary would like to join, as well as reducing inflation risks.
As a result of the change, the central bank's net foreign currency position will be zero with the central bank's reserves equalling its foreign currency debts, the Finance Ministry said earlier.
The AKK said it planned to finance Hungary's budget from domestic issues until 1998.
It added that the planned changes will still enable the NBH to take up loans for its on account after January 1.
